plugins.name: finsharpe
plugins.description: FinSharpe's hosted MCP servers for Indian capital-markets work plus eight research and advisory skills (stock, MF, ETF, portfolio X-ray, market summary, client comms, report studio, instructions builder) in one Claude Code plugin.

skills.name: client-communications
skills.description: Draft any client-facing communication for the FinSharpe advisory practice across channels: emails (onboarding, review invitations, market commentary, fee/renewal notes, difficult conversations like drawdowns or delays), review-meeting summaries, portfolio explainer notes for non-finance audiences, and broadcast vs individual messages — with the right tone, compliance posture, and none of the tells that make a message read as AI-written. Use this skill whenever the user wants to "write to a client", "draft an email", "explain this to the client", "send a review summary", "inform clients about", handle an unhappy client, or make any client-facing draft "sound more human" — even when the channel isn''t named. For short WhatsApp messages specifically, this skill routes to client-whatsapp-comms which owns that channel. Do NOT use for internal notes, marketing copy for the platform, or branded PDF deliverables (finsharpe-report-studio).
headings: The anti-AI-tell pass (run on every draft)

skills.name: etf-analyst
skills.description: Analyse ETFs and index funds the way passive vehicles must be analysed: tracking error and tracking difference against the underlying index, market price vs iNAV premium/discount, on-exchange liquidity and impact cost, AUM viability, expense ratio, and the special risks of international ETFs in India (unit-creation suspensions under overseas investment limits, wide premiums). Use this skill whenever the user asks about an ETF, index fund, "passive fund", tracking error, premium/discount, "ETF vs index fund", gold or silver ETFs, or international ETFs like MAHKTECH/MON100 — even if they call it just "a fund", if the vehicle is passive this skill applies. Do NOT use for actively managed mutual funds (mf-analyst) or single stocks (stock-analyst).

skills.name: finsharpe-report-studio
skills.description: Render white-labelled, brand-consistent FinSharpe deliverables: IPS, financial plan report, risk-profile summary, allocation and product one-pagers, review decks, plus research deliverables (equity research notes, MF and ETF reports, portfolio X-ray reports, market briefings from the analysis skills), all built to the FinSharpe design system (cream, forest green, gold; Fraunces / Inter / IBM Plex Mono) with optional white-labelling to a partner''s branding. Use this skill whenever the user wants to "produce the report", "make it look professional", "brand this", "white-label it", "build the client PDF / deck", or turn any planning or analysis output into a polished document. Trigger it as the final stage after ips-builder or any analysis skill, whenever a FinSharpe-branded PDF, Word doc, deck or workbook is the deliverable. It owns palette, fonts, layout, cover pages, PDF build settings, the research provenance footer, and the no-em-dash house style.
headings: 1. Read the design system and confirm branding mode
2. Pick the format and the underlying skill
House style (enforced here for the whole pipeline)

skills.name: market-summary
skills.description: Produce a data-grounded Indian market summary at any cadence: morning brief, end-of-day wrap, weekly note, or event-driven commentary. Pulls the market overview, advance-decline breadth, institutional (FII/DII) flows and derivatives positioning from the FinSharpe MCP toolkit and composes it for the chosen audience and channel. Use this skill whenever the user asks "what''s happening in the market", "market update", "how did markets do today/this week", "morning brief", "FII flows", "market positioning", or wants market commentary drafted for clients or a newsletter — even a casual "kya chal raha hai market mein". Do NOT use for single-stock news (stock-analyst) or fund questions (mf-analyst).
headings: 3. Compose for the audience and channel

skills.name: mf-analyst
skills.description: Run the FinSharpe mutual fund research workflow: resolve a scheme, analyse its holdings history and manager behaviour, place it in category context via the screener, check the correct TRI benchmark, and produce a factual scheme note or a category-level quantitative scan. Use this skill whenever the user names a mutual fund scheme or MF category and wants analysis, a review, "is this fund good", holdings changes, manager churn, category comparison, overlap between funds, or a quantitative look at a category (e.g. arbitrage funds, smallcap funds) — even if they just paste a scheme name with a question mark. Do NOT use for ETFs or index funds where tracking mechanics matter (etf-analyst), single stocks (stock-analyst), or whole-portfolio diagnosis (portfolio-xray).
headings: Snapshot            ## What the manager is doing (holdings history)
Points to note      (mandate drift, AUM, manager changes — factual flags)

skills.name: portfolio-xray
skills.description: Diagnose an existing portfolio of stocks and/or mutual funds: parse the holdings, resolve every symbol and scheme, then run the full X-ray — concentration (stock, sector, market-cap, AMC), fund overlap, quality and red-flag screen on underlying names, per-asset risk contributions via the quant toolkit, cost drag, and gap versus a target allocation if one exists. Use this skill whenever the user shares a list of holdings (typed, pasted, or in a file/statement) and asks any whole-portfolio question: "review my portfolio", "what''s wrong with this portfolio", "am I too concentrated", "analyse these holdings", "X-ray this", "check overlap in my funds", or a prospect''s incoming portfolio during onboarding. Do NOT use for building a fresh allocation from scratch (asset-allocation-architect) or single-security questions (stock-analyst / mf-analyst / etf-analyst).
headings: What you actually hold      (look-through summary, cap/sector split)
Quality screen              (weight in flagged names, with the flags)
Risk decomposition          (top risk contributors vs their weights)
Summary of findings         (numbered facts, no prescriptions)

skills.name: stock-analyst
skills.description: Run the full FinSharpe single-stock research workflow for any NSE-listed company: resolve the symbol, pull fundamentals, scores, technicals and institutional ownership from the FinSharpe MCP toolkit, check recent filings, run the red-flag screen (PAT growth, leverage, pledging, cash conversion), and produce a factual research note or branded report. Also handles head-to-head stock comparisons (2-3 names, aligned metrics, no winner declared). Use this skill whenever the user names a stock and wants analysis, research, a deep dive, a "view", fundamentals, a health check, red flags, "what''s going on with X", or a comparison like "X vs Y" — even if they don''t say "research" or "report" explicitly. Do NOT use for portfolio-level questions (portfolio-xray), mutual funds or ETFs (mf-analyst / etf-analyst), or options positioning (that is F&O analysis).
headings: Snapshot          (what the company does, market cap tier, industry position)
Fundamentals      (growth, margins, returns — with peer percentile context)
Ownership & flows (institutional holders, direction of change)
Red-flag screen   (each check, pass or flag, with the number behind it)
What to watch     (upcoming triggers: results date, pending orders, rating reviews)

skills.name: system-instructions-builder
skills.description: Turn a recurring FinSharpe task or workflow into a reusable instruction artifact: a Claude skill (SKILL.md), Claude Project instructions, an API system prompt, or a FinSharpeGPT agent spec — written in FinSharpe house conventions (anti-fabrication, no recommendations, SEBI compliance language, MCP-tool delegation, design system references). Use this skill whenever the user says "turn this into a skill", "make a prompt for this", "write system instructions", "I keep doing this manually", "build an agent for X", "make this repeatable", or wants to capture a workflow from the current conversation into something reusable. Also use it to review or tighten an existing prompt or skill. Do NOT use for one-off task execution — this skill builds the instructions, it does not perform the underlying task.
headings: Step 3: Draft to the house template
